title: Uncertainty relations for arbitrary currents in coherent transport
abstract: We derive thermodynamic and kinetic uncertainty relations valid for arbitrary currents in coherent, strongly coupled, linear systems out of equilibrium. Exploiting properties of the transport statistics, in particular fluctuation theorems, we identify the relevant entropy production and activity that determine the cost of precision at the level of individual scattering events. The resulting bounds include higher-order fluctuations and remain valid far from equilibrium. We illustrate our results in normal and superconducting hybrid structures, and show that their predictiveness and validity range exceeds existing formulations.
summary: This work develops generalized uncertainty relations for quantifying the fundamental limits of precision when measuring various currents (energy, charge) in coherent quantum transport. By incorporating fluctuation theorems and analyzing strongly coupled regimes, the authors extend existing bounds to be valid far from equilibrium. This is crucial for understanding non-equilibrium energy dissipation and measurement constraints in advanced quantum devices like superconducting junctions.
main_problem: The paper derives generalized thermodynamic and kinetic uncertainty relations for quantifying precision limits associated with arbitrary currents flowing through coherent, strongly coupled quantum systems out of equilibrium.
main_result: New bounds (TUR, KUR, and a combined TKUR) are established that remain valid far from equilibrium and extend beyond previous limitations restricted to particle or charge currents. These bounds show higher-order fluctuation contributions when strong coupling is present.
method: The derivation relies on applying the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality to transport statistics, specifically utilizing properties derived from fluctuation theorems (e.g., forward-backward stochastic entropy).
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on coherent fermionic transport in linear systems, illustrated using normal-normal (NN) and normal-superconducting (NS) hybrid junctions.

important_parameters: Strong coupling regime, far from equilibrium, superconducting leads (Andreev reflections).
main_assumptions: The derivation assumes the current statistics can be analyzed via scattering theory and that particle-particle interactions are negligible or treated in a mean-field manner.

paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the general framework for uncertainty relations based on transport statistics, deriving specific forms for TUR and KUR applicable to arbitrary currents, introducing a generalized Thermokinetic Uncertainty Relation (TKUR), and finally validating these results using superconducting hybrid structures.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous, non-equilibrium bounds on measurement precision in quantum conductors, which is highly relevant for understanding energy/charge transport dynamics beyond simple linear response theory.
